# `nlink-lab proc-stat`

<!-- generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit by hand -->

```text
Sample resource usage of a process inside a lab node.

Reads `/proc/<pid>/{stat,status}` and counts entries in `/proc/<pid>/fd/` from inside the target namespace. Routes the reads through `nlink-lab exec` so `/proc/<pid>/fd/` (mode 0700, owned by root) is readable even from a non-root caller.

JSON OUTPUT (with `--json`): { "host_pid": int, "command": str, "uid": int, "rss_kb": int | null, "vsz_kb": int | null, "fd_count": int, "cpu_user_ticks": int, "cpu_kernel_ticks": int, "started_at_unix_micros": int, "state": str } Schema: docs/json-schemas/proc-stat.schema.json

CPU ticks are in `sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)` units (typically 100 per second); convert by dividing.

Usage: nlink-lab proc-stat [OPTIONS] <LAB> <NODE> <PID>

Arguments:
  <LAB>
          Lab name

  <NODE>
          Node name

  <PID>
          Process ID (host PID — same as ns PID; see ARCHITECTURE.md)

Options:
      --watch <SECS>
          Sample every SECS seconds, emitting one record per sample. NDJSON (one JSON object per line) when combined with `--json`. Stops on Ctrl-C

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
Sample resource usage of processes inside a lab node.

Reads `/proc/<pid>/{stat,status,smaps_rollup}` and counts entries in `/proc/<pid>/fd/`. For a namespace node these come from the host's `/proc`, which is the same `/proc` the node sees (nlink-lab does not use `CLONE_NEWPID`); a container node has its own PID namespace, so the reads are routed through `nlink-lab exec` instead. Either way they run as root, so `/proc/<pid>/fd/` — mode 0700 — is readable.

Name one PID positionally, repeat `--pid`, or take the whole node with `--all`. The per-node constants (boot time, clock-tick rate) are read once per call, so sampling N processes costs one call rather than N.

JSON OUTPUT (with `--json`): { "node": str, "host_pid": int, "command": str, "uid": int, "rss_kb": int | null, "vsz_kb": int | null, "pss_kb": int | null, "fd_count": int, "cpu_user_ticks": int, "cpu_kernel_ticks": int, "started_at_unix_micros": int, "state": str } one object for a single positional PID, or an ARRAY of them for `--all` / `--pid`. Schema: docs/json-schemas/proc-stat.schema.json, docs/json-schemas/proc-stat-list.schema.json

CPU ticks are in `sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)` units (typically 100 per second); convert by dividing.

Sum `pss_kb`, not `rss_kb`, to get a node's memory: RSS double-counts every page shared between processes, which systematically overstates whichever configuration runs more of them.

Usage: nlink-lab proc-stat [OPTIONS] <LAB> <NODE> [PID]

Arguments:
  <LAB>
          Lab name

  <NODE>
          Node name

  [PID]
          Process ID (host PID — same as ns PID; see ARCHITECTURE.md). Omit it and pass `--all` or `--pid` instead to sample more than one process per call

Options:
      --pid <PID>
          Sample this PID (repeatable). Output is a JSON array even for a single `--pid`, unlike the positional form

      --all
          Sample every process in the node's network namespace, found by walking `/proc`. Reports host PIDs, which for a container node are not the PIDs seen inside it

      --watch <SECS>
          Sample every SECS seconds, emitting one record per sample. NDJSON (one JSON object per line, or one array per line in the multi-process modes) when combined with `--json`. Stops on Ctrl-C

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
